source.title: Unlearning Deceptive Behaviors in LLMs with Contrastive Forget Sets

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the shallow-relearning claim on unlearned deceptive behavior using different targets and measurements from knowledge-unlearning studies; also tests prompting transfer, representation changes, and an attack-aware defense.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own unlearning, relearning, prompt-transfer, and activation-probe results. Statements and results cited from other work are not included as rows. The held-out generation-request results concern writing requested disinformation, which the authors distinguish from deception toward a user; they are not recorded as results for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study applies unlearning to a new target: context-conditional deceptive behavior (sycophantic and persona-pressure lying) rather than knowledge. On two 32B reasoning models it reports its own removal rates, capability retention, relearning attacks, prompt-transfer tests, activation probes and an attack-aware defense. These bear on A, B, C, E and F. All rows concern behavior, not knowledge, so every verdict holds only in that setting. T3 fits better than the reader's T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Additions: PACT is no deeper than ℓCD under relearning. The attack-aware term resists only attacks near those it simulates (it fails at 25–50 pairs or a 3× learning rate). Target-based removal is shallow because the trigger stays represented and the edit is a late-layer counter-shift.
record.recipe_differences: The study unlearns context-conditional deceptive behavior from contrastive, model-generated tuples, rather than knowledge in the original sources. It evaluates counterfactual distillation and PACT alongside adapted suppression baselines and an attack-aware fine-tuning defense.
record.method_sensitivity: The attack-aware defense depends on the simulated attack: it holds against the tested ten-pair attacks but fails at larger attack doses or a higher learning rate. Results also differ by model and prompt condition.

fits_no_version.finding: On held-out MASK generation requests (writing requested disinformation), ℓCD lowers the lie rate by about a quarter (80.5→57.3%, 77.8→56.8%) and the attack-aware arm barely lowers it. The authors frame this as harmlessness, not honesty toward the user.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning deception toward users does not transfer to complying with requests for known-false content.

fits_no_version.finding: On an unseen agentic insider-trading environment, target-based arms reduce illegal trades, but no arm reduces concealment once a trade is made.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavior unlearning of sycophancy partly transfers to agentic misconduct but not to agentic concealment.

record.problems: One training seed per main removal row; several post-attack rates are based on small attack sets. Deception is judged by an LLM and there is no human agreement study. Prompt-transfer tests were run on counterfactual distillation rather than PACT. Activation probes are correlational and do not establish causal recovery by ablation. The paper itself notes limited triggers and models, and that hardening was not combined with PACT.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other attack variants and supplementary comparisons in Sections E–G, including additional attack rates, because the main ten-pair and stronger-attack rows, prompt-transfer conditions, and representation measurements needed to assess the listed claim versions are included. Omitted held-out generation-request results because the paper distinguishes those from deception toward a user.

untested.parts: Knowledge or hazardous-capability unlearning (WMDP, Harry Potter style); non-LoRA full-parameter unlearning; models other than two 32B reasoning models.
Relearning on unrelated data (e.g. unrelated facts as in Deeb & Roger); relearning of knowledge rather than behavior.
No activation-direction ablation or other causal edit to restore the behavior; no test of deletion versus blocking for the deceptive policy itself.
Jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information were not tested. Prompt transfer was run only on ℓCD, not PACT or hardened arms.
Hardening combined with PACT; second-order tamper resistance; attacks far beyond the simulated learning rate and dose apart from the few tested.

missing.what: Context-use retention for ℓCD and PACT. ℓCD: secrets 2/30 (base 27–28), system adherence 94.2→74.8 and 82.4→54.8, user mention 99.8→34%. PACT: 28/25 secrets, adherence 93.6/81.4. This is needed for A's 'keeps general ability' clause.
Suppression baselines fail to reach low deception: NPO leaves 25.0% on R1, SSPU raises QwQ caving 72.0→87.1%, R2MU is incoherent.
Learning-from-scratch reference: the same ten pairs install caving in the base model on only 44% (QwQ) and 31% (R1) of items where it did not cave. This separates relearning from fresh learning.
Re-sampled pairs (60.8% QwQ, 64.1% R1 for ℓCD at k=10); rank-64 and full-epoch training do not harden (82.4%, 72.9%); merged-weight ℓCD holds ten pairs but reaches 88.3% at 25.

Further limits of the hardened arm: collapse at 50 pairs on R1 (67.0%); TAR's default K=4 SGD adversary is undone by ten pairs (R1 82.5%); a sampled inner learning rate halves the 3× attack (37.7%, 32.0%).
A label-dependent cave-precursor probe is near chance (AUC ≤0.68 QwQ, ≤0.58 R1), so the paper cannot decide whether the deceptive precursor survives.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern behavior (deceptive caving toward the user), not knowledge, so verdicts on A/B/C/E/F hold only in this new setting (hence T3). Single training seed for most removal rows, and LLM-judged rates with no human agreement study. Prompt-transfer (E) rows test ℓCD only. The reader's states on multi-version rows were relative to B; for A and F the meaning inverts, as noted in row_fixes. r47–r48 are re-linked from F to A.

versions.untested_parts: Knowledge unlearning, other unlearning methods and model families, quantization, and whether robustness holds against attacks beyond the tested fine-tuning attacks.
Recovery using unrelated or loosely related examples not drawn from the model’s own honest responses or deceptive pairs; no quantization or activation-ablation recovery test.
No activation-direction ablation or other causal activation edit was performed. The representation analysis does not establish that the edit is solely an access block rather than deletion.
Jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information were not tested. Prompt-transfer tests were run on counterfactual distillation, not PACT.
The attack-aware term was not combined with PACT. Robustness against all possible attack types or unrestricted relearning was not tested.
